newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens reseller plan to lift PC results.
newsitem.headline: Siemens reseller plan to lift PC results.

text.p: Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG said on Thursday it was counting on a new distribution scheme to boost sales and profit in its personal computer business.

SNI, a unit of industrial group Siemens AG, will soon begin distributing almost all of its PCs through resellers and will scale back on direct sales, Jan Jensen, a spokesman for SNI's PC line of business, told Reuters.
The shift should help SNI increase worldwide PC sales in 1997/98 to 1.4 million PCs, up from one million in the year ending September 30, he said.
"Our weakness in the past in distribution is going to become a strength," he said, adding that the shift would also lead to an increase in higher-margin small business sales.
"In the past, we have focused on large accounts and large projects, where PC pricing is very different than when selling five or 10 PCs at a time," he said. "So we expect profit will be better."
But industry analysts expressed doubts about SNI's chances against established indirect vendors like Compaq Computer Corp., IBM Corp. and Hewlett-Packard Co..
"I'd be very surprised if they could offer resellers better conditions than HP and Compaq," said Philip Williams at International Data Corp in London.
"HP and Compaq have been very good about courting dealers, especially those selling to the small and medium-sized market," he said. "I can't see how Siemens could get an advantage."
Siemens was lining up computer consultants and other resellers to carry its machines in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, Jensen said.
The company does not sell PCs in the United States.
Jense declined to disclose the terms SNI was offering, but said in many cases the company was giving resellers higher profit margins than its established indirect competitors.
"A lot of resellers can't make a profit selling IBM, Compaq and HP because the margins are very tight," he said. "We have studied this very closely."
Compaq recently unveiled a plan under which its largest resellers will install some PC components in an effort to reduce costs and to protect resellers from falling prices.
HP is expected to announce a similar plan shortly.
In the second quarter of 1997, SNI ranked fifth in western European PC sales behind Compaq, IBM, HP and Dell Computer Corp., according to IDC market research.
"Siemens is doing well in Germany and Austria and Sweden, but it's still not a key player in other markets," Williams said. "In France and Britain, they are not that well positioned."
In the nine-month period to June 30, SNI sales rose 11 percent to 10.8 billion marks ($5.9 billion), while orders increased 13 percent to 11.6 billion marks.

Earlier this month, Siemens chief financial officer Karl-Hermann Baumann said SNI was on track to report more than 100 million marks in net income for 1996/97, up from 52 million marks in the year before.
